name: Coursera AI integrity policy
dinh_nghia: Coursera's AI Academic Integrity policy is a multi-layered framework announced June 2024 that combines AI-generated post-submission viva-style questioning, plagiarism detection (Turnitin integration), and proctoring (Honorlock) to verify authentic student learning in an era of generative AI. The flagship feature is the 'AI-based Viva Exam': after a student submits a written assignment, AI analyzes the submission and generates custom follow-up questions that require the student to demonstrate genuine understanding of their own work — a digital analogue of the academic oral defense.
phan_loai: Coursera's AI integrity framework addresses: (1) AI-assisted dishonesty — post-submission dialogue reveals whether the student can explain and defend AI-generated content; (2) Plagiarism — Turnitin integration detects textual similarity before and after submission; (3) Cheating in proctored assessments — Honorlock lockdown browser prevents unauthorized resource access; (4) Identity fraud — proctoring verifies test-taker identity. The AI Viva Exam is particularly novel: it targets AI-assisted ghostwriting by requiring real-time cognitive demonstration, not just artifact analysis.
lich_su_khai_niem: Coursera announced its AI academic integrity suite in June 2024, following a reported surge in AI-assisted cheating on its platform since ChatGPT's release in November 2022. The AI Viva Exam concept builds on Coursera's existing 'Coach' chatbot functionality. Partnerships with Turnitin (plagiarism detection) and Honorlock (proctoring) were pre-existing and maintained alongside new AI integrity tools. The announcement came alongside other AI features including AI-Assisted Grading and Proctoring improvements.
ten_truong_hop: Coursera AI Academic Integrity Suite, launched June 2024. Pilot institutions: select universities in India, Malaysia, and the United States. Vietnam pilot: FPT University and Van Lang University. Global platform with 148 million registered learners (2024). Partners: 325+ universities and companies offering content on Coursera.
dien_bien: Coursera's June 2024 announcement described a GenAI-powered Academic Integrity suite comprising: (1) AI-based Viva Exam — after submission, AI analyzes free-form written assignments and grading criteria to dynamically generate custom follow-up questions testing authenticity and critical thinking behind the student's submission; students must respond to these questions, and responses are reviewed alongside the original submission; (2) AI-assisted grading with plagiarism context; (3) Enhanced Turnitin integration — students can see similarity scores before final submission and amend work; (4) Honorlock proctoring — lockdown browser for high-stakes assessments. Vietnam pilot: Coursera piloted its academic integrity tools at FPT University and Van Lang University as part of the broader Asia-Pacific rollout, with specific attention to AI-assisted academic misconduct in online degree programs.
ket_qua_xu_ly: The AI Viva Exam approach is preventive and formative rather than purely punitive: students who cannot answer follow-up questions about their own submission receive flags for educator review rather than immediate academic sanctions. Turnitin integration: when similarity score exceeds threshold, assignment is flagged and student receives plagiarism policy reminder requiring signature acknowledgment. The combined system provides educators with richer evidence for academic misconduct investigation than text analysis alone. Pilot outcomes not yet published in peer-reviewed literature as of 2025. [uncertain]
con_so_thong_ke: Coursera: 148 million registered learners globally (2024). 325+ university and industry partners. Number of institutions participating in the academic integrity pilot: not publicly disclosed beyond India, Malaysia, US, Vietnam. [uncertain] No published data on false positive/negative rates of the AI Viva Exam system as of 2025. [uncertain] Turnitin: processes over 200 million student submissions annually globally.
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: Post-submission AI questioning creates a new cognitive demand on students — they must be prepared to explain their submitted work at any time. For students who engaged genuinely, this is a low-burden reinforcement of understanding. For students with test anxiety, the unexpected follow-up may be stressful. There is a potential false-positive risk: a student who wrote their own work but struggles to articulate it under pressure may be unfairly flagged. Accessibility considerations for non-native English speakers answering follow-up questions in English are important given Coursera's global learner base.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: Coursera's AI Viva Exam represents an applied instantiation of the 'post-submission authentication' concept in educational research. If effective and scalable, it could influence the design of online assessment integrity globally. The lack of published peer-reviewed evaluation of the system's accuracy and fairness is a significant gap. The risk of algorithmic bias in how follow-up questions are generated or evaluated is not publicly addressed. [uncertain]
hai_cho_xa_hoi: Positive: restores confidence in the value of online credentials by demonstrating authentic learning verification. Coursera credentials are widely used in professional hiring; if perceived as vulnerable to AI cheating, their value collapses. Negative risk: the post-submission dialogue requirement may disadvantage disadvantaged learners who have genuine knowledge but struggle with on-demand verbal/written elaboration. May also create false equivalence between Coursera's certificates and traditional university degrees if integrity systems are not rigorously validated.
cong_cu_phat_hien: Coursera's multi-tool detection framework: (1) Turnitin AI detection — integrated into Coursera's submission pipeline; detects similarity to known sources and AI-generated content patterns; (2) AI Viva Exam — custom question generation post-submission to test authorship; (3) Honorlock — live proctoring, lockdown browser, identity verification for high-stakes exams; (4) Internal AI plagiarism detector — Coursera announced development of proprietary AI detection tool (Inside Higher Ed, June 2024). The AI Viva Exam is unique: it shifts detection from artifact analysis to cognitive demonstration.
han_che_cong_cu: Turnitin AI detection: documented false positive rates, especially for ESL writers (Liang et al., Stanford 2023: 61.3% for non-native writers). Honorlock: can be bypassed by determined cheaters using secondary devices. AI Viva Exam: the quality of follow-up questions depends on the quality of the AI's analysis of the submission — if the submission is generic AI text, the follow-up questions may also be generic and easy to answer without genuine understanding. The system cannot catch sophisticated actors who used AI to generate content AND then studied that content thoroughly. No independent validation of the AI Viva Exam's effectiveness has been published. [uncertain]
watermarking: Coursera does not implement LLM watermarking. Watermarking (Kirchenbauer/UMD, Aaronson/OpenAI) would be complementary to Coursera's detection suite — if AI providers implement mandatory output watermarking, Coursera's Turnitin integration could detect watermarked AI-generated text with higher reliability. The AI Viva Exam is a parallel approach that authenticates the student rather than analyzing text artifacts.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: The AI Viva Exam fundamentally changes Coursera's assessment model: assignments are no longer evaluated solely on the submitted artifact. The viva element creates a two-stage assessment: (1) written submission, (2) follow-up dialogue. This design mirrors process-based assessment recommendations from academic integrity researchers (Perkins et al., 2023; Eaton, 2024). For instructors, the AI-assisted grading feature provides rubric-aligned analysis, reducing grading time while maintaining quality oversight. The combination is intended to make AI-assisted dishonesty riskier and less reliable for students.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: Coursera partners with 325+ universities, each with their own academic integrity policies. The Coursera platform policies (plagiarism acknowledgment signature, Turnitin integration) apply platform-wide. The AI Viva Exam feature is available to institutional partners who opt in. Vietnam institutions: FPT University and Van Lang University adopted Coursera's AI integrity features as part of their AI governance frameworks for online learning programs. Exact scope of adoption at each institution is not publicly detailed. [uncertain]
van_hoa_to_chuc: Coursera's approach is detection-and-verification-heavy rather than honor-code-cultural. The platform operates at massive scale (148M learners) where relationship-based trust is not feasible — it must rely on systemic mechanisms. The AI Viva Exam introduces a social element (dialogue) that partially addresses the anonymity problem of online assessment. Requiring students to be accountable for explaining their work in dialogue (even with an AI) is more honor-code-adjacent than purely surveillance-based.
ai_literacy: Coursera offers dedicated courses on AI literacy and ethics, including 'Generative AI for Students: Ethics & Academic Integrity' (available on the platform). The AI Viva Exam feature may inadvertently increase AI literacy: students who experience post-submission AI questioning learn that AI can analyze and probe their understanding, which may encourage more genuine engagement with assignments. Coursera's policy communications (plagiarism reminders, academic integrity training) constitute structured AI literacy interventions for learners.
khung_quoc_te: Coursera's AI integrity suite aligns with UNESCO 2023 guidance on AI in education (assessment redesign, transparency). The Turnitin partnership links to broader international debates about AI detection reliability. The EU AI Act (2024) Annex III classifies AI used in educational assessment as high-risk where it determines access or evaluation — Coursera's AI Viva Exam may fall under this classification for partner universities in EU jurisdictions. Compliance status not publicly addressed. [uncertain]
phap_luat_viet_nam: Coursera is used extensively in Vietnam, including by FPT University and Van Lang University (explicit pilot sites for the AI integrity features). Vietnam's Nghị định 109/2022/NĐ-CP (Điều 20) establishes academic integrity requirements without specific mention of AI tools or online learning platforms. No MOET directive specifically governs the use of Coursera's AI integrity features in accredited programs. FPT and Van Lang adoption suggests institutional-level policy acceptance.
chinh_sach_chau_a: FPT University and Van Lang University (Vietnam): pilot sites for Coursera's AI integrity features. Indian and Malaysian universities: also pilot sites per Coursera's June 2024 announcement. NUS (Singapore): uses Coursera for some programs but has its own AI policy framework (2023/2024 disclosure framework). The Asia-Pacific focus of Coursera's pilot rollout reflects the region's large online learner population and documented concerns about AI-assisted cheating in high-volume online programs.
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: Coursera's AI Viva Exam represents a systemic attempt to shift AI from 'cheating enabler' to 'integrity verifier' — using AI to ask the questions that expose AI-assisted work. This is consistent with Rose Luckin's (UCL) argument that AI can democratize education: the AI Viva Exam makes personalized assessment (follow-up questioning) scalable in a way that human-only vivas cannot be for 148 million learners. Neil Selwyn's concern about AI undermining educational authenticity is directly addressed by the post-submission dialogue mechanism.
edtech_company_policies: Coursera AI Academic Integrity suite (June 2024): (1) AI-based Viva Exam — dynamically generates custom follow-up questions from submitted work, tests authenticity and critical thinking; (2) Turnitin integration — similarity detection with pre-submission student review option; (3) Honorlock proctoring — lockdown browser and identity verification; (4) AI-assisted grading — rubric-aligned submission analysis; (5) Plagiarism acknowledgment signature. Vietnam pilot: FPT University and Van Lang University. Global pilot: select institutions in India, Malaysia, USA.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: From an EdTech researcher perspective: (1) Coursera's AI Viva Exam is an important innovation in online academic integrity — it should be rigorously evaluated in peer-reviewed research for accuracy, fairness, and student experience impact; (2) The Vietnam pilot (FPT, Van Lang) provides a valuable research opportunity for Vietnamese EdTech researchers to study AI integrity mechanisms in a national context; (3) The combination of Turnitin + Honorlock + AI Viva represents a layered defense approach consistent with best practices; (4) Risk: over-reliance on any single AI detection mechanism creates arms-race dynamics — the layered approach is more robust; (5) Institutional adoption should include student communication about the post-submission dialogue feature to maintain transparency and trust.

No peer-reviewed Vietnamese academic publication on this pilot as of 2025. [uncertain] Vietnam context: Nghị định 109/2022/NĐ-CP, Điều 20 (academic integrity in scientific activities). Springer 2024 study on AI use among 1,386 Vietnamese students provides relevant background on the scale of AI-assisted academic dishonesty in Vietnam.
